## Background


Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are *tons* of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-built data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
Now with **ggplot**:

First I need to install the package with `install.packages()`

> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot)` in my quarto document as this will result in me *re-installing* the package every time I render my report

Every time I want to use a function from a given package, I need to load it with a `library()` call:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)

```

Every ggplot needs at least **3** things:

-The **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
-The **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
-The **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist)+
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE,) +
  theme_gray() + 
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)", 
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)", 
title="Claire's Plot of Stopping Distances")
```
## Gene Expression Plot

read the data from online:
```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```
```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2,col=State) + 
geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue", "grey", "red")) +
  labs(title = "Gene expression Changes Upon Drug Treatment", subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo", x="Control (no drug)", y="Drug Treatment")
myplot

```
> Q. How many genes are in this dataset?


```{r}
nrow(genes)

```

> Q. How many are "up" regulated?

```{r}
#genes$State
```
```{r}
table(genes$State)
sum(genes$State == "up")

```
> Q. What percentage of genes are "down regulated?

```{r}
sum((genes$State == "down")/(nrow(genes)) *100)


n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.down <- sum(genes$State == "down")

ans <- round(n.down/n.total *100, 4)
ans
```
The percentage of down genes is `r ans`% and that is that...

We can install extra packages with `install.packages()` like **patchwork**

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
      p4

(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)
```
```{r}
myplot + 
  facet_wrap(~State)
```
## The GapMinder data
The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lots of stuff we can plot :)
```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

< Q. How many data entries are there in this data set?

```{r}
head(gapminder)
nrow(gapminder)
```
> Q. How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))

```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp,) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.33)
```
Adding in color 
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, colour = continent) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.33) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```
Histograms of 
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram()
```
Boxplot

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
